label: CATL Headquarters & Gigafactory
sub: Ningde, Fujian, China — World's largest single battery maker; >600 GWh/yr capacity. Produces LFP, NMC, NMCA, and sodium-ion cells. Home of Kirin and Shenxing battery R&D.

label: Tesla Gigafactory Nevada
sub: Sparks, Nevada, USA — Panasonic-Tesla JV. Produces 2170 cylindrical cells for Model 3/Y and Powerwall/Megapack. Opened 2016; expanded multiple times. ~40 GWh/yr capacity.

label: Tesla Gigafactory Texas
sub: Austin, Texas, USA — Opened April 2022. First production site for Tesla's 4680 tabless cylindrical cells and structural battery packs. Produces Cybertruck and Model Y. ~100 GWh/yr target.

label: Tesla Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg
sub: Grünheide, Germany — Inaugurated March 2022. Produces Model Y for European market with structural battery packs. First Tesla factory outside the Americas. ~500,000 vehicles/yr target.

label: Northvolt Revolt Ett — Skellefteå (now Lyten)
sub: Skellefteå, Sweden — First European-owned gigafactory (first cell Dec 2021). Filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy Nov 2024. US battery startup Lyten completed acquisition of the Ett site plus Northvolt Labs (Västerås) on Feb 27, 2026, establishing its first European Industrial Hub; NMC cell supply resumed for BESS use, with a co-located data center campus (with EdgeConneX) planned to scale to 1 GW.

label: LG Energy Solution — Ochang Campus
sub: Ochang, North Chungcheong, South Korea — Major LGES production hub for cylindrical and pouch cells. Supplies Tesla, GM (Ultium), Stellantis. After landmark Jan 2022 IPO, LGES is now second-largest battery maker globally.

label: Samsung SDI — Cheonan Factory
sub: Cheonan, South Korea — Major Samsung SDI prismatic and cylindrical cell production. Partners with BMW, Stellantis, Rivian. Leading solid-state battery R&D program targeting 2027–2030 pilot production.

label: BYD Headquarters & Blade Battery Production
sub: Shenzhen, Guangdong, China — Home of BYD's corporate HQ and key R&D campus. Blade Battery (LFP) invented and commercialized here (2020). BYD is now the world's largest EV maker by volume and a top-3 battery maker.

label: Volkswagen PowerCo — Salzgitter
sub: Salzgitter, Lower Saxony, Germany — VW's battery subsidiary PowerCo SE established 2022. Unified prismatic cell production targeting 40 GWh/yr. Anchor of VW's six-gigafactory European plan.

label: Toyota Solid-State Battery R&D — Toyota City
sub: Toyota City, Aichi, Japan — Toyota holds ~1,000 solid-state battery patents — more than any other automaker. Sulphide solid electrolyte pilot production began early 2025. Targeting 2027–2028 commercial EV with 1,200 km range.

label: QuantumScape — San Jose, CA
sub: San Jose, California, USA — Stanford spin-off backed by VW and Bill Gates. Lithium-metal solid-state separator pioneer. IPO via SPAC in 2020, briefly valued at $50B. Achieved automotive-format cell spec in 2024 (QSE-5).

label: Argonne National Lab — Battery Research
sub: Lemont, Illinois, USA — US DOE national lab and home of the Joint Center for Energy Storage Research (JCESR). Leads US government-funded battery research including lithium-sulfur, lithium-air, and solid-state chemistries. Budget >$120M/yr in battery R&D.

label: Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT)
sub: Suwon, Gyeonggi, South Korea — Samsung's flagship research center. Key solid-state battery research including sulphide electrolyte and lithium-metal anode. Published peer-reviewed solid-state cycle-life breakthroughs. Works closely with Samsung SDI on commercialization.

label: Atacama Salt Flat — Lithium Brine
sub: Atacama, Antofagasta, Chile — World's largest lithium reserves (~37% global supply) in brine deposits. SQM and Albemarle produce lithium carbonate here. Chile nationalized lithium industry in 2023 (CODELCO joint ventures). ~200,000 tonne LCE/yr capacity.

label: Pilbara — Hard Rock Lithium Spodumene
sub: Pilbara, Western Australia — World's largest hard-rock lithium source. Pilbara Minerals, Albemarle (Greenbushes), and IGO operate mines. Australia is the world's largest lithium producer by volume (~50% of global mine supply). Spodumene is processed into hydroxide for NMC batteries.

label: DRC Cobalt Belt — Katanga
sub: Katanga Province, Democratic Republic of Congo — Source of ~70% of global cobalt. Glencore (Katanga Mining) and Chinese companies (CMOC) are dominant operators. Human rights abuses in artisanal mining (ASM) operations have prompted automakers to require supply chain due diligence and accelerate cobalt-free battery development.

label: Moss Landing BESS — 3 GWh
sub: Moss Landing, Monterey County, California, USA — Vistra Energy's facility is the world's largest grid-scale battery (3 GWh after Phase 3 expansion, 2025). Uses Tesla Megapacks. Replaced two gas peaker plants. Demonstrates 4-hour discharge for 300,000+ homes.

label: Hornsdale Power Reserve — Neoen/Tesla
sub: Jamestown, South Australia — Built in 2017, Neoen's Hornsdale Power Reserve was the world's first large-scale lithium-ion grid battery (150 MW / 194 MWh). Proved grid storage commercial viability. Expanded in 2020 to 300 MW / 394 MWh. Demonstrated frequency response 140× faster than gas turbines.

label: US Department of Energy — Washington, DC
sub: Washington, DC, USA — DOE administers the IRA's $3B battery manufacturing grants, the 45X production tax credit, and the Loan Programs Office (LPO) financing for battery factories. JCESR and Battery500 Consortium funded by DOE. Under Biden administration, issued $10B+ in battery facility loans.

label: European Commission — Brussels
sub: Brussels, Belgium — EU Battery Regulation (2023) mandates digital battery passport, carbon footprint disclosure, and recycled content minimums. European Battery Alliance (EBA250) coordinates EU gigafactory strategy. EU Critical Raw Materials Act (2024) targets 10% domestic extraction of battery minerals by 2030.

label: FAMU-FSU Engineering — Zinc-Ion Battery Research
sub: Tallahassee, Florida, USA — Florida A&M / Florida State University College of Engineering. April 2026: published non-flammable hydrogel-based zinc-ion battery (MnO₂ cathode / PVA-aramid electrolyte) sustaining 900+ cycles. Water-based manufacturing avoids dry-room requirements, targeting grid-scale and residential backup storage.

label: HyperStrong — CATL Sodium-Ion Grid Deal
sub: Shenzhen, China — Energy storage integrator HyperStrong signed a 60 GWh, three-year sodium-ion battery supply agreement with CATL in April 2026 — the world's largest Na-ion order on record. Projects span grid-scale BESS deployments across China. Validates sodium-ion economics for stationary storage.

label: California Grid Storage — 17 GW Installed
sub: Sacramento, California, USA (CAISO) — May 5, 2026: California's battery storage fleet discharged 12,000 MW during peak evening hours — equivalent to 12 large nuclear plants — meeting over 40% of state demand. 17,000+ MW of cumulative installed BESS capacity makes California the world's largest grid-scale battery market. Replaced ~5,000 MW of retired gas peakers since 2022.

label: Togg EV — CATL CAIT Bedrock Platform
sub: Gemlik, Bursa, Turkey — Turkey's government-backed EV brand Togg partnered with CATL's CAIT skateboard chassis division in May 2026 to jointly develop the Bedrock platform for a B-segment vehicle family. CAIT's first overseas passenger EV platform project; targets European and MENA markets with sub-€35,000 pricing.

label: CATL Fuding — Sodium-Ion Gigafactory
sub: Fuding, Fujian, China — CATL's dedicated sodium-ion production hub. Sixth phase announced May 9, 2026: ¥5 billion investment adding 40 GWh of Na-ion capacity, bringing total site capacity to 149 GWh. Produces 2nd-gen cells targeting ~200 Wh/kg at LFP-comparable cost — powering the world's largest sodium-ion supply deal (60 GWh with HyperStrong).

label: Copwood VFB Energy Hub — Europe's Largest Vanadium Flow Battery
sub: East Sussex, England, UK — Invinity Energy Systems' Copwood VFB Energy Hub: Europe's largest vanadium flow battery installation at 20.7 MWh (90 units). Commissioned May 2026 under the UK government's Longer Duration Energy Storage (LDES) programme. Co-located with a 3 MW solar array; water-based electrolyte with no fire risk; 8+ hour discharge duration.

label: Moment Energy — Second-Life Battery Megafactory
sub: Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada — Moment Energy's Megafactory 1, billed as the world's largest second-life EV battery repurposing facility, held its ribbon-cutting and went operational on June 23, 2026 — just six weeks after being announced. Targets 1 GWh/yr of BESS capacity by 2030 from repurposed retired EV packs, serving data centers, hospitals, and microgrids; 100+ direct and 1,000+ indirect BC jobs expected. Companion facility to the primary gigafactory under construction near Austin, Texas.

label: Gotion High-Tech — Gnascent Na-Ion HQ
sub: Hefei, Anhui, China — Headquarters and R&D center of Gotion High-Tech (26.5% owned by Volkswagen Group). On May 17, 2026, Gotion launched the 'Gnascent' sodium-ion battery brand at its 15th Global Technology Conference: high-energy variant at 261 Wh/kg (closing the gap with NMC), grid-storage variant rated 20,000+ cycles, both targeting mass production Q4 2026. First Western-backed sodium-ion supply chain to reach commercial production scale outside CATL.

label: Ganfeng Lithium — Solid-State Production Hub
sub: Xinyu, Jiangxi, China — Ganfeng Lithium, China's largest lithium producer, began small-batch production of 500 Wh/kg solid-state lithium-metal battery cells in May 2026 — a world first at this production stage. The 400 Wh/kg variant has completed 1,100+ cycle validation. Targets premium EVs, eVTOL aircraft, drones, and robotics.

label: Spearmint Energy Red Egret — 600 MWh BESS
sub: Texas City, Texas, USA — Spearmint Energy's 300 MW / 600 MWh standalone battery energy storage system in the ERCOT market. Closed $450M in project financing in May 2026 (First Citizens Bank, Investec, Nuveen, ITC transfer proceeds). Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 hardware; commercial operations targeted 2027.

label: Basquevolt — 402 Wh/kg Lithium-Metal Battery
sub: Vitoria-Gasteiz, Basque Country, Spain — Basquevolt launched the BQV400L cell on May 22, 2026: 402 Wh/kg, 8.9C pulse power, 10–80% charge in under 15 minutes. Uses hybrid polymer solid electrolyte. Manufactured in Spain with 75% European-sourced components. Renault Ampere JDA confirmed. First credible European-owned solid-state-adjacent cell at competitive energy density.

label: Lyten — Former Northvolt Drei Site, Heide
sub: Heide, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany — Lyten signed an exclusive MOU on Jul 1, 2026 with KfW and Northvolt Drei Project GmbH to acquire this 110-hectare brownfield gigafactory site (~€60M) where Northvolt broke ground in 2024 but never began construction. Lyten plans a smaller-scale facility (~1,000 jobs vs. 3,000 originally planned) combining cell production, energy storage, and a data center; definitive agreement targeted for Q3 2026.

label: Gigafactory Malaysia — Sepang
sub: Suria Industrial Park, Sepang, Selangor, Malaysia — NanoMalaysia Bhd subsidiary Gigafactory Malaysia Sdn Bhd launched small-scale EV and energy-storage battery production in mid-July 2026 using a domestically-developed "graphite-enhanced" lithium-ion chemistry (MYR 20M / ~US$5M R&D). Billed as Malaysia's first local battery technology production facility and the first of its kind in ASEAN.

label: ProLogium — Solid-State Gigafactory, Dunkirk
sub: Dunkirk, Nord, France — ProLogium Technology's European solid-state gigafactory, backed by €1.5B in French government and EU regional funding. Mass production ramp targeted Q2 2029. ProLogium (Taiwan) announced a $3.8B Nasdaq SPAC listing (ticker: PRLG) in May 2026 to fund the facility. Targets EV, data center UPS, aerospace, and robotics markets with 360 Wh/kg 4th-generation cells.

label: Wolfsberg Lithium Project
sub: Carinthia, Austria — Europe's first fully permitted lithium mine, owned by European Lithium. Critical Metals Corp's proposed acquisition (targeting September 2026 close) would give the combined company direct access to European road/rail infrastructure and reduce EU dependence on imported lithium spodumene.

label: Saudi Arabia — 2 GW/8 GWh BESS Program
sub: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia — Saudi Power Procurement Company awarded $1.16B in build-own-operate contracts (Aug 20, 2026) for four standalone battery storage projects (Haden, Al-Muwayh, Al-Khahfah, Al-Khushaybi) totaling 2 GW/8 GWh, the first tender of its kind in the Kingdom. Led by ACWA Power-Saudi Energy and Engie consortia.

label: CATL Debrecen Cell Plant
sub: Debrecen, Hungary — CATL's largest planned manufacturing base outside China (100 GWh capacity). Began trial cell production Sep 22, 2026 after clearing an August nickel-exposure safety suspension; has produced 537,000 battery modules since autumn 2024.

label: PowerCo St. Thomas Gigafactory
sub: St. Thomas, Ontario, Canada — Volkswagen subsidiary PowerCo's $7B cell plant, delayed two years to a 2029 operational start (from 2027) to accommodate next-gen battery technology. EllisDon Corporation named general contractor Sep 24, 2026; ~60 workers on site, scaling to ~1,300 at peak.

label: Kasaragod Solar+BESS, Kerala
sub: Kasaragod, Kerala, India — 100 MW solar park with co-located battery energy storage system (BESS) approved by Kerala government October 2026. Part of India grid-scale storage deployment push.
